collections/repetition#

Repeats values lazily or as a finite sequence.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

for Repeating(value: "tick") -> value {
    output.writeln(value);
    last if clock.expired();
}

Description#

Repeats values lazily or as a finite sequence.

Repeating is infinite. Its cursor is always available, so consumers must impose their own stopping condition:

Repeated is finite, indexed and sized:

let padding = Repeated(value: " ", count: 4);
// padding.size() == 4
// padding.item(2) == " "

A negative count throws InvalidArgument. item() uses strict zero-based bounds and throws OutOfRange. first() and last() throw EmptySequence when count is zero.

Cycled repeatedly traverses a finite Sequencing value:

let turns = Cycled(origin: players);
for turns -> player {
    player.move();
    last if game.finished();
}

Cycling an empty sequence is finite and immediately exhausted. Cycling a non-empty sequence is infinite. Every cursor is immutable.
